theory.title: Exercise 2.3.3: Suite-Level Test Template
theory.content:
MENTOR-9: "Sometimes an entire test file is dedicated to one type of validation—API response codes, database queries, calculation results. In those cases, use Test Template in Settings to avoid repeating [Template] in every test case."

Test Template in Settings

Test Template in *** Settings *** applies to ALL test cases:

*** Settings ***
Test Template    Validate Response

*** Test Cases ***
Test Case 1
    endpoint1    200
    endpoint2    200

Test Case 2
    endpoint3    404
    endpoint4    500

Difference from [Template]:

  • Test Template (Settings): Applies to ALL tests in file
  • [Template] (Test level): Applies to ONE test only
  • No need to repeat [Template] in each test
  • Entire file becomes data-driven

Example: Calculation Validation Suite

*** Settings ***
Test Template    Should Be Equal

*** Test Cases ***
Addition Tests
    ${2 + 2}    ${4}
    ${10 + 5}   ${15}
    ${100 + 1}  ${101}

Multiplication Tests
    ${2 * 3}    ${6}
    ${5 * 5}    ${25}
    ${10 * 0}   ${0}

Subtraction Tests
    ${10 - 5}   ${5}
    ${20 - 15}  ${5}

Three test cases, all using Should Be Equal from Test Template. No [Template] tags needed.

⚠️ Test Template Best Practices

  • Use when ALL tests in file use same template
  • Individual tests can override with [Template] NONE
  • Great for: validation suites, regression tests, batch checks
  • Keeps test file focused on data, not structure
  • Can still mix templated and non-templated tests (use NONE)
  • More maintainable for large data-driven test files
